parsed.explanation: No trans-specific offence, targeting, facility ban, or violence is documented, and the same-sex statute (14 years) is recorded as unenforced with no prosecutions in official and advocacy reporting. That makes criminalisation a secondary, latent risk, not an active campaign. However there is no documented social acceptance of trans people, no functioning visitor recourse, and no trans-specific data at all; enforcement evidence is dated 2010-2013 with no recent sourcing, and official rhetoric opposes recognition citing the penal code. In this thin-data context silence is not safety. It therefore sits a step below acceptance-plus-protections cases, but above jurisdictions with documented universal exposures or organised targeting.
